# How Hydrogen Water May Support Brain Protection During Surgery

Hydrogen water might help protect young children's brains during surgery. This could make medical procedures safer for babies and kids.

## What the Research Shows

Scientists found that hydrogen gas helped protect baby brain cells from damage caused by sevoflurane. Sevoflurane is a common medicine used to make patients sleep during surgery. The [original research study](/study/correction-to-inhalation-of-hydrogen-gas-mitigates-sevoflurane-induced-neuronal-apoptosis-in-the-neonatal-cortex-and-is-associated-with-changes-in-protein-phosphorylation-1777577956392) showed hydrogen reduced brain cell death in young animals. This research adds to the growing body of [hydrogen general research](/blog/category/general) showing brain protection benefits.

The study focused on preventing [anesthesia-induced neurotoxicity](/explore-by-condition/anesthesia-induced-neurotoxicity). This means protecting the brain from harmful effects of anesthesia medicines. Hydrogen also helped reduce [neuronal apoptosis](/explore-by-condition/neuronal-apoptosis), which is when brain cells die in a programmed way.

## How Hydrogen Water Delivery Works

Molecular hydrogen (H2) is a tiny gas molecule that can reach the brain easily. While this study used hydrogen gas that patients breathed in, hydrogen can also be delivered by drinking hydrogen-rich water. Water ionizers and hydrogen water machines like those from Echo Water™ dissolve H2 gas directly into drinking water.

The hydrogen molecules are so small they can cross the blood-brain barrier. This barrier normally protects the brain from harmful substances. But it also blocks many helpful treatments. Hydrogen's tiny size lets it reach brain cells where it may provide protection.

## How to Apply This for Brain Health

While this study used inhaled hydrogen gas, drinking hydrogen water may offer similar brain protection benefits. Here's how to use hydrogen water for potential brain health support:

**Daily Amount:** Drink 1-2 glasses of hydrogen-rich water per day. Each glass should contain 12-16 ounces of water.

**Timing:** Drink hydrogen water on an empty stomach for best absorption. Try first thing in the morning or between meals.

**Consistency:** Use hydrogen water regularly rather than just occasionally. The brain benefits may build up over time with consistent use.

**Before Medical Procedures:** If you or your child has surgery planned, talk to your doctor about hydrogen therapy options. Some hospitals are studying hydrogen gas for surgery protection.

## What to Look For in Hydrogen Water Quality

Not all hydrogen water machines create the same quality water. Here's what makes good hydrogen water:

**High H2 Concentration:** Look for machines that produce at least 1.0 parts per million (ppm) of dissolved hydrogen. Higher concentrations around 1.5-2.0 ppm are even better.

**Negative ORP Levels:** ORP stands for oxidation-reduction potential. Good hydrogen water should have an ORP between -300 to -600 millivolts. This shows the water has antioxidant power.

**Third-Party Testing:** Choose machines tested by independent labs. This proves the hydrogen levels are real and consistent.

**Fresh Production:** Hydrogen gas escapes from water quickly. The best machines make fresh hydrogen water right when you drink it.

## Key Takeaways for Hydrogen Water and Brain Protection

• **Start early:** Begin drinking hydrogen water regularly to build up potential brain protection benefits over time

• **Quality matters:** Invest in a hydrogen water machine that produces high H2 concentrations above 1.0 ppm for maximum benefit

• **Talk to doctors:** Discuss hydrogen therapy with your healthcare team, especially before any planned surgeries for you or your children

• **Stay consistent:** Drink hydrogen water daily rather than occasionally to maintain steady levels of molecular hydrogen in your system

This research shows promise for protecting young brains during medical procedures. While more human studies are needed, hydrogen water offers a simple way to potentially support brain health. The [hydrogen research database](/proxy/) contains many other studies exploring hydrogen's protective effects on the brain and nervous system.

Remember that this animal study used inhaled hydrogen gas, not hydrogen water. More research is needed to confirm if drinking hydrogen water provides the same brain protection benefits in humans.

**Disclaimer:** Consult your healthcare provider before starting any new health regimen, especially if you or your child has upcoming medical procedures.
